questions.q: What distinguishes an outbound integration from an inbound integration?
options: Outbound integrations are always synchronous; inbound integrations are always asynchronous
In an outbound integration, Salesforce initiates the call to an external system; in an inbound integration, an external system calls into Salesforce
Outbound integrations use Apex; inbound integrations always use Flow
There is no real difference — the terms are interchangeable in Salesforce documentation
questions.explain: The direction is defined by who initiates the call: outbound means Salesforce is the client calling out, inbound means Salesforce is the server being called.

questions.q: Which of these is a declarative (no-Apex) way to make an outbound HTTP callout, available since Spring '23?
options: Apex REST web services
Outbound Messaging
Flow Builder's HTTP Callout action
The webservice keyword
questions.explain: Flow Builder gained a native HTTP Callout action starting Spring '23, letting admins build callouts without writing Apex, using the same Named Credential and External Service building blocks.

questions.q: A business process has Salesforce push a new order to a warehouse system, and later that warehouse system calls back into Salesforce to report a shipment. What does this scenario illustrate?
options: That a single business process can require both outbound and inbound integration
That outbound and inbound integration can never coexist in one business process
That this must be modeled entirely as a Platform Event
That Named Credentials are only relevant to inbound integration
questions.explain: The push to the warehouse is outbound (Salesforce initiates it); the shipment report is inbound (the warehouse system initiates it) — both directions appear in one overall process.

questions.q: What platform rule about callouts is described as shaping "so much integration code"?
options: A transaction can't make a callout while it has pending uncommitted DML, async work, or email in the same transaction
Callouts can only be made from Batch Apex
Every callout must use a Named Credential, with no exceptions
Callouts are limited to exactly one per Apex class
questions.explain: This constraint is why callouts are often sequenced before DML, or deferred into async Apex contexts like @future or Queueable so the save and the callout each run in their own transaction.

questions.q: Which mechanism auto-generates Apex callout code and an invocable Flow action from a third-party API's OpenAPI specification?
options: Change Data Capture
External Services
Outbound Messaging
The webservice keyword
questions.explain: External Services import an OpenAPI (OAS) document and generate the Apex stub classes and invocable action automatically, rather than requiring a hand-written callout.
